subject: Computer Networking
title: Role-Based Access Control
description: A fast breakdown of Role-Based Access Control for builders.

hook.text: Should every employee access every file? Of course not. RBAC ensures people only access what their role requires.

buildup.text: Roles group permissions. An 'editor' can write content. A 'viewer' can only read. An 'admin' can manage users.

discovery.text: Users get roles, not individual permissions. Adding a new hire means assigning one role, not fifty rules.

twist.text: Role explosion is real. Too many fine-grained roles become as unmanageable as individual permissions.

climax.text: Principle of least privilege: give the minimum access needed. If a role doesn't need it, remove the permission.

punchline.text: RBAC matches access to responsibility. Nothing more.

quiz.question: What principle should guide RBAC design?
options: Least privilege — grant only the minimum access needed
Maximum access — let everyone see everything
Equal access — give all users identical permissions

details.summary: Role-based access control assigns permissions to roles rather than individual users, and users are assigned to roles matching their job functions. An accountant gets accounting system access, a developer gets code repository access, and permissions change automatically when roles change.
details.whyItMatters: RBAC enforces the principle of least privilege at scale. Without it, permission management becomes chaotic as organizations grow, leading to excessive access and security vulnerabilities.
takeaways: Permissions are assigned to roles, not individual users
Users inherit permissions by being assigned to appropriate roles
Role changes automatically update all associated permissions

faq.question: How does RBAC differ from other access control models?
faq.answer: Discretionary access control lets resource owners set permissions individually. Mandatory access control uses security labels set by policy. Attribute-based access control makes decisions based on user, resource, and environment attributes.

faq.question: What is the principle of least privilege?
faq.answer: Users should have only the minimum permissions required to perform their job. When someone changes roles, their old permissions are revoked and new ones granted. This limits the damage from compromised accounts because each account can only access what its role specifically requires.
